answer: Every agent identity must anchor to a ferrous stake: a refundable bond locked before the agent can trade, sized so that creating ten fake identities costs ten times the bond while earning nothing extra. Peers then re-check each other's work, and a failed check slashes the bond and revokes the identity. An attacker who wants to reach the zenith of influence must fund a fresh bond for every sockpuppet, and each one risks the same slash, so the cost of faking scales linearly while the gain stays flat.
